headline: 3 val images are byte-identical to 3 train images (labels included) — your validation metrics are untrustworthy; remove the 3 val pairs and re-split before training.
training_impact: Training will run fine, but the model will have memorised 3 of its 135 val images (10 boxes each, ~1.6% of val boxes). Any mAP/precision computed on this val set is inflated by an unknown margin, so you cannot compare checkpoints or decide ship-readiness from it. Fixing this after training means retraining, so do it now.

decisions.rationale: Exact detector, verified against the raw data: val/218885329401, val/706346898744 and val/916278631571 are sha1-identical to train/000000221754, train/000000336232 and train/000000277005 respectively, and the label files match row-for-row. This is not a near-duplicate or a false positive — the model will be graded on images it trained on. Fix: delete the 3 val image+label pairs (or move them to train) and re-split; then re-run the audit before training. Everything else is clean: no missing/orphan/empty labels, no malformed rows, no corrupt images, no out-of-bounds/degenerate/tiny boxes, no denormalised coordinates, no class-id errors.
